key_insight: Manually curated EHR features, especially when paired with NLP, produced the strongest acute pancreatitis detection, but a simpler automated approach using maximum lipase also performed nearly as well.
clinical_relevance: For clinical phenotyping and surveillance, carefully chosen lab-based proxies can substantially reduce manual effort while preserving useful identification performance.
method: Built and tested two ML approaches on EHR data for acute pancreatitis detection.
Compared a custom model using manually curated structured data, validated outcomes, and optional NLP features versus a highly automated model using low-cost silver-standard labels.
Evaluated performance with cross-validated AUC and predictive performance at a fixed PPV threshold.
evidence_signal: Custom structured-data models achieved cv-AUC 0.89 and improved to 0.91 with NLP, while the automated model reached AUC 0.80 using diagnosis-code count and 0.88 using maximum lipase; at 90% PPV, sensitivities were 92%, 45%, and 84%, respectively.
watch_item: Automated phenotyping can depend heavily on phenotype-specific proxies like lab thresholds, so portability and label quality may vary across sites and EHR systems.
paper_title: A Comparison of Manual and Automated Approaches to Developing Computable Algorithms for Identifying Acute Pancreatitis
